name: Chitin
prior: Nonlinear plates in real time exist in research and a few tools: Bilbao/Webb/Wang/Ducceschi 'Real-Time Gong Synthesis' (DAFx 2023; Foeppl-von Karman, explicit energy-quadratised/SAV scheme, pitch glides + crashes, real-time on a CPU) [VS: dafx.de/paper-archive/2023/DAFx23_paper_19.pdf; physicalaudio.co.uk/modelling-gongs]; Ducceschi & Touze modal method with wave-turbulence cascade (2015) [VS: researchportal.ip-paris.fr]; nlm - open-source Max externals for real-time non-linear modal synthesis of strings, membranes and plates (Diaz/Constanzo/Sandler, PdMaxCon25, arXiv 2603.10240, github.com/rodrigodzf/nlm) [VS: arxiv.org/abs/2603.10240]; Chair Audio EXC!TE CYMBAL (free VST3; Hit Position, Tip Hardness, Bell, Choke; PRO 25 EUR adds 'Non-linearity', Timbre, Spread, sidechain excitation) [VS: chair.audio/product/excte-cymbal; rekkerd.org; cdm.link]; Physical Audio Modus (plates connected by nonlinear springs/rattles, 'nonlinear plate reverberation' via sidechain in 1.3) and Derailer (FDTD strings/bars/nonlinear springs) [VS: synthanatomy.com/?p=75001; kvraudio.com/product/derailer-by-physical-audio]; Physical Audio note: Berger's simpler model gives pitch glides but not the energy spread needed for crashes [VS: physicalaudio.co.uk/modelling-gongs]. Not found: any touch/phone instrument with Chladni-position strike, held rubbing into turbulence, or playable pitch sag. In Myzel: Gong fakes the bloom with delayed fades and a settling bend [APP 3796-3812], Schale/Glocke linear.
costNotes: 16 complex resonators in a worklet measured 0.61 units incl. node = ~0.034 per resonator [R: webaudio.md s4] -> 12 modes 0.41, 24 modes 0.82. Doublets (+-0.3%) double the count: 12 'modes' as doublets = 24 resonators -> read the spec as 12 resonators total (6 doublet pairs) or budget 0.8 for 24. Cascade: u = sum, nl = b*u^3/(1+u^2) (~6 flops) and 12 weighted injections ~15 ns = 0.12; exciter (noise table x y + telegraph particles) 0.05; node 0.06 + 3-4 k-rate params 0.1. Pitch sag = per-block cos/sin per mode (12-24 trig calls per block) negligible but must be lerped. L1 ~0.75-0.8 at 12 resonators; L3 24 modes + quadratic term + stereo ~1.6-1.7. With doublets at L1 add 0.4. Chrome FTZ covers denormals; still flush states per block [R s3].
soundHeld: The strike + rub mapping on one finger is the strongest idea in this batch: at rest the plate rings linearly, with pressure it goes into sag + shimmer, and rubbing is a textural drone that no Myzel engine has. But the cascade as specified is not wave turbulence: a scalar cubic of the mode sum fed back into the same 12 modes is waveshaped feedback - it adds intermodulation products that land ON the existing 12 resonances (k-weighted), so it brightens and distorts rather than spreading energy into hundreds of new frequencies. Physical Audio says the same about Berger-class models (glide yes, crash no). With 12-24 modes a 'crash' is impossible; the honest result is 'gong with pitch sag and growing shimmer', which is still new for a phone. Fix: inject band-limited noise scaled by rms(u)^2 into the upper modes (turbulence proxy) and let the cubic only drive the sag. Pitch sag with eps*rms^2 per block gives the right downward glide after a hard hit; it must be lerped per sample or it zippers (idea knows).
soundBurst: Struck Puls hits work well: position (y) gives five instruments from one note as claimed, since |sin(pi m y + phi)| really kills modes at nodal lines - but with only 12 modes and strongly stretched f_k = f(1+ck)^1.3 the sound can be thin and clangy compared with Gong's PeriodicWave groups; the doublets and T60 spread are needed, not optional. Gate = Chick/open is good (Exc!te Cymbal's Choke is popular). Failure: at Puls density the cubic feedback never drains -> each hit adds energy, sag drifts downwards and level rises until the energy cap bites, i.e. a pumping drone instead of hits; cap by per-voice energy AND decay the nonlinearity gain with the envelope.
failureModes: Cubic feedback into resonators with gain above loss self-oscillates or explodes; saturating form + per-block energy cap + beta*rms^2 clamp <= 0.8 are mandatory, and must be tested at f = 60 Hz and 4 kHz
The 'cascade' is intermodulation onto existing modes, not turbulence: no crash, only shimmer/distortion; add rms-gated noise into high modes
Pitch sag per block zippers (planned lerp) and, under Bebung, detune and sag fight: compute w_k from (f*detune)*(1-eps*rms^2) in one place
Doublets double resonator count; cost 0.8-1.2 at L1 depending on reading, L3 1.7+ (Gong is 1.55 today, so Chitin is the most expensive worklet engine)
Modes above 0.45*SR must be dropped per note (high f * k^1.3 stretch exceeds Nyquist quickly at 24 modes); mode count becomes pitch dependent -> level normalisation per note
Rubbing drone = noise x y into a linear bank sounds like Hauch through Schale unless the stick-slip/telegraph particles are convincing; needs listening iteration
Puls at density: energy accumulates across hits, drone instead of hits; tie nonlinearity gain to the envelope
verdict: Rare: real-time nonlinear plates exist as research code (DAFx 2023 gong, nlm Max externals 2026) and as a 'Non-linearity' knob in Chair's cymbal plugin and Physical Audio's Modus, but nothing playable on a phone with Chladni-position strikes, rubbing into chaos and pitch sag under the finger. Feasible as a worklet at about 0.8 units (1.7 at level 3, doublets extra), the most expensive engine of the batch. The strike/position/choke side will sound distinct and musical; the cubic 'cascade' as written is waveshaped feedback that brightens but cannot crash, and it is the main stability risk. Build it with a hard energy cap, an rms-gated noise turbulence proxy, and sell the sag + shimmer honestly rather than promising crashes.
